answer: The network tags every identity with a public pigment mark recording its provenance, and each identity must anchor itself to a deposit held in escrow by an unrelated custodian: the deposit sits on a ledge, released only after the identity survives a full epoch of public scrutiny. A proven fraud finding tips the escrow to the challenger, so one honest agent risks one deposit once, while a sybil farmer must fund a separate anchored escrow for every fake and loses them all the moment one is exposed.
